# The Banach–Tarski Paradox

## Thesis

**Banach–Tarski**: a ball in 3D can be split into finitely many pieces and rigidly reassembled into two balls of the same size. Pieces are non-measurable; the proof uses the **Axiom of Choice**. Conceptual chapter — not a physical claim about oranges.

## Mental model

```text
  ball → AC pieces → isometries → two balls
  volume only for measurable sets
```

## Worked examples

### What fails without Choice / in 2D

Analogous finite decompositions fail in $\mathbb{R}^2$ with isometries; without Choice the pieces need not exist.

### Where Choice shows up

Free groups inside $SO(3)$ and Choice-picked orbits yield non-measurable pieces (see Wagon).

## Trap

**Using Banach–Tarski as an engineering gotcha.** It does not break energy conservation; volume is undefined for those pieces.

## Boring rule

Stay in Lebesgue-measurable sets when you need volume.

## Try this

1. Read the free-group paradox (Hausdorff).
2. Compare Vitali sets.
3. Skim Wagon, *The Banach–Tarski Paradox*.
